answer: Glacier-delta identity sharding. Each agent gets a short-lived credential seeded by a public VRF over the epoch's beacon; the VRF output partitions agents into delta shards, and only one agent per shard per epoch may act. An attacker must predict the unpredictable beacon to pre-mine positions, but shard assignment stays hidden until reveal. To hold k shards they must run k full identities over many epochs, paying real compute and latency for each concurrent slot while gaining only a fractional share. Ivory-listed anomalies trigger re-sharding without operator penalties, just lost slots.
